description:
User requests backend persistence of strict attachment delivery failure; display belongs to a later PR. Audit completed with module-context skill and applicable lifecycle/Agent/Engine/Channels policies. No code changes made. Implementation explicitly STOPPED by supervisor under user no-drift constraint pending the contract decision below.

A. Mental model: Agent.Api.prepare_response_context reserves/finalizes the canonical assistant UUID and body before schedule_return_hop sends through Channels. The answer is already stored; generation completion is separate from delivery.
B. Responsibilities: Conversations/ExecutionLifecycle own generation finalization/private execution; DeliveryConfirmation forwards confirmed receipts; History.Delivery interprets provider-confirmed transport; HistoryIngress/TranscriptHistory own confirmation, fixed target association and recovery.
C. Dependencies: existing NodeRouter Engine events carry normalized outgoing IDs/receipt; Engine Repo owns messages/executions/transcript placements. Channels must not write Engine persistence directly.
D. Contracts: errors are data-only DeliveryError facts with safe message/stage/certainty and redacted original reason. DeliveryConfirmation.record currently returns all errors unchanged. Engine exposes record_delivery_confirmation but NO delivery-failure/outcome recording operation today.
E. State: Message stores canonical assistant identity/body and private metadata; ExecutionRecord terminal completed means generation completed and is immutable. TranscriptMessage stores association/provenance but no failed delivery state. Public history strips Message metadata/private traces.
F. Failure trace: admitted input -> reserved assistant ID -> Conversations.finalize_successful_message persists assistant/completed root -> Channels strict preparation/upload abort -> DeliveryError returned/logged -> failure facts are not persisted or associated.
G. Invariants: preserve original assistant UUID/body/source identity; do not change completed generation to failed; do not mark transport confirmed, fabricate provider IDs/audience, invoke success callback or resend; nil actor/IDs never grant mutation authority; safe bounded metadata only, no raw errors/bytes/handles/credentials.
H. Risks: TranscriptHistory.associate_prepared requires delivery_confirmation and stamps provider_confirmed provenance. Direct/Shared targets derive from admitted input; Replicated email recipients derive from confirmed envelope evidence. Reusing success association for aborted mail would fabricate scope and could expose private undelivered content or feed it back as ordinary agent history.
I. Existing tests: DeliveryConfirmation unit tests preserve errors/no success recording; History.Delivery/HistoryIngress/TranscriptHistory tests cover confirmed association/recovery; strict SMTP and Mattermost integration cases prove zero publication. Future private-outcome regression should finalize a real admitted assistant first, trigger strict failure through existing delivery path, assert same Message ID/body and bounded failure metadata, no confirmation/placement/send/callback; reject mismatched input/assistant/connector scope and verify idempotent replay/recording failure preserves original transport result. Do not author/alter those contracts until decision.
J. Pending decision: private failure evidence on EXISTING assistant message versus a distinct failed transcript-placement contract. Private metadata alone preserves the failed answer/evidence but does NOT create a TranscriptMessage placement or satisfy literal public-transcript visibility. Any placement requires separately agreed authorized targets, failed provenance and history-consumption semantics.

Minimal proposed backend extension (NOT implemented): Channels reports normalized strict failure through an explicit Engine failure/outcome operation in the existing delivery-reporting path; History.Delivery validates the persisted admitted-input/assistant pair and original connector scope and stores safe metadata on that same assistant via an Engine-owned metadata-only changeset. Preserve error/no-resend response. Keep public transcript placement confirmation-only. No Agent lifecycle, transport, UI, new registry/queue or retry framework changes.

Action reuse assessment: existing finalize_incoming, DeliveryConfirmation, record_delivery_confirmation, History.Delivery, Message metadata changeset and TranscriptHistory association inspected; none records failure. Extend existing delivery-reporting owner/NodeRouter lifecycle with explicit failure semantics only if approved. Internal transport bookkeeping is local-only, not an agent/workflow operation or new exposed Action/tool. Existing confirmed-only operation cannot truthfully be called success for a failure.

Supervisor explicitly instructed to stop implementation, record this audit/proposal, and ask user about private outcome persistence with failed placement/display deferred. Prior dirty code and test state preserved; no tests/application checks needed for this Beadwork-only audit.

comments.text: User explicitly deferred transcript failure persistence in favor of connected notification workflow coverage. Audit remains evidence only; no code changes or failed transcript association authorized.
